Maggie's approach is a bit different: self trained, she likes to keep her style simple and natural, letting the food speak for itself and the skills of the photographer really shine through.

programme.title: Paula McIntyre's Hamely Kitchen
programme.desc: S2 E1 Paula adds a modern twist to a traditional roozle breid, a variation on potato bread, by transforming it into a taco.

programme.title: Home Cooking Made Easy
programme.desc: S1 E3 Entertaining Lorraine prepares a gorgeous, hearty Spanish paella with sherry, chorizo, and prawns - the ideal one-pan 'help yourself dish' for a fun night in with friends and family.

programme.title: Pati's Mexican Table
programme.desc: S12 E9 Pink An ingredient Pati constantly uses is salt and Yucatan has one of the most unique salts. The Las Coloradas salt, which means blush red, gets its distinctive color from red algae. Engineer Felipe Perez takes Pati to the pink lakes where the salt is produced. Down the road in Rio Lagartos, conservationist Diego Nunez takes her to see another pink wonder, Mexico's highest concentration of flamingos.

programme.title: David Rocco's Dolce Italia
programme.desc: S1 E2 Old Venice on the Water David sets out with his family to get the true Venice tourist experience and meets a charming gondolier and his wife, who teach them all about the history and pride of the age-old tradition of the gondolas in Venice. They explore local hotspots and venture off the beaten path to a beautiful Venetian winery, sampling gourmet cicchetti along the way. David then spends time with Emanuel, a local fisherman,.

programme.title: Island Echoes with Nornie Bero
programme.desc: S1 E8 Echoes of Erub In the final episode of Season 1 of Island Echoes, Nornie Bero visits the breathtaking island of Erub to experience a truly unique local pastime.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing: Simply Provence
programme.desc: S1 E9 Chocolate There is one delicious food that is adored across the world. It may have started life in South America as the humble cocoa bean, but it's the Swiss, Belgians and French, who've turned it into an ingredient we all adore.

programme.title: My Market Kitchen
programme.desc: S6 E19 Mike is joined by his daughter Abigail to whip up her favourite treat, double chocolate cookies. Matt creates a Vietnamese dessert, coconut creme caramel. Laura wraps up the show with carbonara.

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen
programme.desc: S8 E8 Wheat Harvest and Pasta Lidia talks the hard work involved with making flour, then bread and pasta. She makes croutons with a Caesar salad, then a fusilli with spinach and herbed ricotta, and a lagane pasta with chickpeas.

programme.title: Tastes And Traditions
programme.desc: S1 E9 In this cozy episode of Tastes and Traditions, we revisit two timeless classics of Ukrainian home cooking-warm, fragrant Cabbage Buns and juicy Pork Cutlets.

programme.title: Jamie at Home
programme.desc: S1 E9 Pizza Jamie searches for edible wild mushrooms in a local forest with his mentor, Gennaro Contaldo. Then he uses them to make bruschetta, risotto and venison Stroganoff.

programme.title: Food Safari
programme.desc: S1 E3 Portuguese Maeve O'Meara takes you on a journey within your very own kitchen and makes new flavours familiar. In tonight's episode, Maeve explores the world of Portuguese food.

programme.title: The Chocolate Queen
programme.desc: S2 E6 Warm apple tarts are hard to resist and pastry expert Kirsten Tibballs is in the kitchen showing her version that's easy to replicate at home. She's also dishing up a brilliant no-churn chocolate, date and ice cream cake that is better than anything you'll find in the store.

programme.title: Everyday Gourmet with Justine Schofield
programme.desc: S4 E33 Justine makes her sweet potato and ginger gratin, gives you some great tips for steaming eggs and Adam Liaw makes his leche flan.

programme.title: The Cook Up with Adam Liaw
programme.desc: S7 E81 Tinned Tomatoes A pantry staple becomes the hero tonight as Adam and his guests, comedian Mel Buttle and chef Dom Wilton make magic with tinned tomatoes.

programme.title: New York Gourmet With Justine Schofield
programme.desc: S1 E5 Justine visits another iconic Buffalo venue for a traditional roast beef lunch before setting off for the breathtaking 1000 Islands, visiting scenic spots like Boldt Castle and Morgan Island.

programme.title: Memory Bites with Matt Moran
programme.desc: S1 E5 Courtney Act Chef Matt Moran delves into the food memories of multifaceted entertainer Courtney Act, revealing how retro family dishes and deep resilience have illuminated their path to stardom.

programme.title: Paula McIntyre's Hamely Kitchen
programme.desc: S2 E2 Paula rustles up a sandwich or 'piece' as it is known in Belfast, but first she has to catch the filling. She joins father-and-son fishing duo, Gerry and Daniel McNally to fish.

programme.title: Home Cooking Made Easy
programme.desc: S1 E4 Simple Lorraine brings the taste of Spain to the table with her Rioja braised lamb shanks with chorizo and garlic, served with her buttery fast-baked mashed potato.

programme.title: Pati's Mexican Table
programme.desc: S12 E10 A Mayan League of Their Own Pati discovers Yucatan's league of their own. She joins the Amazonas, a softball team of Indigenous women, for their morning practice. As they built a name for themselves, they overcame the mindset that women belong in the kitchen. After teaching Pati the ins and outs of the game, Dona Enedina invites her over for Brazo de Reina, a tamal with hardboiled eggs and ground pepitas.

The Honeymooners, The Andy Griffith Show and Roseanne all offer funny snapshots at class divisions in America, divisions that are even starker in Arrested Development and Schitt's Creek. But it is It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia that asks the hardest, perhaps funniest question of all - is this aspirational game we're all playing rigged against us?

programme.title: NFL Classics: After Further Review
programme.desc: S1 E3 2010 AFC Divisional: Jets VS. Patriots In a historic upset, the Jets shock Brady's Patriots in Foxborough. Bart Scott and hip-hop icon Method Man hold no punches rewatching the wild game.

programme.title: Normal People
programme.desc: S1 E7 As Connell comes to terms with tragic news from home, he battles his own demons and seeks help in rebuilding his life. Marianne continues to offer Connell support after she returns to Sweden.

programme.title: NHK World English News
programme.desc: English news from Japan's Broadcasting Corporation, NHK, delivering the latest in business, technology, health, environmental and world news.

programme.title: Al Jazeera News Hour
programme.desc: In-depth global news from Al Jazeera Satellite Network, Doha, Qatar, in English.

programme.title: New York Gourmet With Justine Schofield
programme.desc: S1 E5 Justine visits another iconic Buffalo venue for a traditional roast beef lunch before setting off for the breathtaking 1000 Islands, visiting scenic spots like Boldt Castle and Morgan Island.

programme.title: Memory Bites with Matt Moran
programme.desc: S1 E5 Courtney Act Chef Matt Moran delves into the food memories of multifaceted entertainer Courtney Act, revealing how retro family dishes and deep resilience have illuminated their path to stardom.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Seafood Odyssey
programme.desc: S1 E1 Suffolk and Naples Contemplating life over a bottle of wine against the backdrop of the bay of Naples, Rick has found the perfect place, and person, to start his seafood odyssey.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Seafood Odyssey
programme.desc: S1 E2 India and Cornwall Rick flees the restaurant to seek comfort from the sea. Forty-eight kilometres out of Padstow, he calms down. Veteran fisherman Ivan Bates introduces Rick to the joys of fishing for the best fish in the world, turbot.

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: S22 E7 South Wales: Richard It's the second night of the competition and the turn of account executive Ricard to host, not in his house but next door in the pub he runs with his partner.

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: S22 E8 South Wales: Daffyd Third to host in South Wales is hotel receptionist and aspiring personal trainer Daffyd, who's hosting a healthy vegetarian-ish dinner party, as he hopes to impress his guests.

programme.title: The Cook Up with Adam Liaw
programme.desc: S7 E81 Tinned Tomatoes A pantry staple becomes the hero tonight as Adam and his guests, comedian Mel Buttle and chef Dom Wilton make magic with tinned tomatoes.

programme.title: The Cook and the Chef
programme.desc: S4 E12 The Art of Presentation Maggie gives us a snapshot on the world of food photography, one which is often veiled in trickery, sprays, glues and gels, all used to artificially enhance the look of a dish. Maggie's approach is a bit different: self trained, she likes to keep her style simple and natural, letting the food speak for itself and the skills of the photographer really shine through.

programme.title: Paula McIntyre's Hamely Kitchen
programme.desc: S2 E1 Paula adds a modern twist to a traditional roozle breid, a variation on potato bread, by transforming it into a taco.

programme.title: Home Cooking Made Easy
programme.desc: S1 E3 Entertaining Lorraine prepares a gorgeous, hearty Spanish paella with sherry, chorizo, and prawns - the ideal one-pan 'help yourself dish' for a fun night in with friends and family.

programme.title: Pati's Mexican Table
programme.desc: S12 E9 Pink An ingredient Pati constantly uses is salt and Yucatan has one of the most unique salts. The Las Coloradas salt, which means blush red, gets its distinctive color from red algae. Engineer Felipe Perez takes Pati to the pink lakes where the salt is produced. Down the road in Rio Lagartos, conservationist Diego Nunez takes her to see another pink wonder, Mexico's highest concentration of flamingos.

programme.title: David Rocco's Dolce Italia
programme.desc: S1 E2 Old Venice on the Water David sets out with his family to get the true Venice tourist experience and meets a charming gondolier and his wife, who teach them all about the history and pride of the age-old tradition of the gondolas in Venice. They explore local hotspots and venture off the beaten path to a beautiful Venetian winery, sampling gourmet cicchetti along the way. David then spends time with Emanuel, a local fisherman,.

programme.title: Island Echoes with Nornie Bero
programme.desc: S1 E8 Echoes of Erub In the final episode of Season 1 of Island Echoes, Nornie Bero visits the breathtaking island of Erub to experience a truly unique local pastime.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing: Simply Provence
programme.desc: S1 E9 Chocolate There is one delicious food that is adored across the world. It may have started life in South America as the humble cocoa bean, but it's the Swiss, Belgians and French, who've turned it into an ingredient we all adore.

programme.title: My Market Kitchen
programme.desc: S6 E19 Mike is joined by his daughter Abigail to whip up her favourite treat, double chocolate cookies. Matt creates a Vietnamese dessert, coconut creme caramel. Laura wraps up the show with carbonara.

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen
programme.desc: S8 E8 Wheat Harvest and Pasta Lidia talks the hard work involved with making flour, then bread and pasta. She makes croutons with a Caesar salad, then a fusilli with spinach and herbed ricotta, and a lagane pasta with chickpeas.

programme.title: Tastes And Traditions
programme.desc: S1 E9 In this cozy episode of Tastes and Traditions, we revisit two timeless classics of Ukrainian home cooking-warm, fragrant Cabbage Buns and juicy Pork Cutlets.

programme.title: Jamie at Home
programme.desc: S1 E9 Pizza Jamie searches for edible wild mushrooms in a local forest with his mentor, Gennaro Contaldo. Then he uses them to make bruschetta, risotto and venison Stroganoff.

programme.title: Food Safari

programme.title: NITV News Update
programme.desc: E61 NITV News recaptures the highlights of Indigenous news around the country.

programme.title: 8 Out of 10 Cats Does Countdown
programme.desc: S13 E11 A hilarious take on Countdown and Letters & Numbers, this hybrid game show hosted by Jimmy Carr is packed with comic appearances, funny mascots, and visual gags.

programme.title: Holy Marvels with Dennis Quaid
programme.desc: S2 E4 Beasts Unleashed Legendary beasts are said to haunt land and sea, terrorising and even possessing humans but are they myth, or is there evidence they've truly wreaked havoc?

programme.title: Great Escapes with Morgan Freeman
programme.desc: S2 E5 Escaping Devil's Island Rene Belbenoit, a petty thief is captured and sentenced to hard time at France's notorious penal colony in French Guiana. He determines to escape or die trying. After many years and numerous harrowing escapes - he finally gets free. His story becomes the basis of several popular movies in Hollywood.

programme.title: The Hospital: In the Deep End
programme.desc: S2 E2 Former tennis pro Jelena Dokic, Hollywood star Ruby Rose, and food writer Matt Preston return to the frontline at St Vincent's, spending time in three demanding departments. Jelena shadows social workers from the domestic and family violence unit, meeting a long-term counselling patient. Ruby experiences the pressures of the ICU, caring for critically ill patients, while Matt sees firsthand the challenges of treating prostate cancer in urology.

programme.title: Hudson & Rex
programme.desc: S8 E6 Conspiracy Theory When a conspiracy podcaster is killed before TruthCon, Mark and Rex enter a shadowy world of theorists where an old comrade with PTSD may hold the key to the murderer.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E8 Movin' On Although the American dream of social mobility underpins America's social contract, that dream is so often beyond reach that it takes sitcom humour to help laugh at the struggles of getting ahead. The Honeymooners, The Andy Griffith Show and Roseanne all offer funny snapshots at class divisions in America, divisions that are even starker in Arrested Development and Schitt's Creek. But it is It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia that asks the hardest, perhaps funniest question of all - is this aspirational game we're all playing rigged against us?

programme.title: NFL Classics: After Further Review
programme.desc: S1 E3 2010 AFC Divisional: Jets VS. Patriots In a historic upset, the Jets shock Brady's Patriots in Foxborough. Bart Scott and hip-hop icon Method Man hold no punches rewatching the wild game.

programme.title: Normal People
programme.desc: S1 E7 As Connell comes to terms with tragic news from home, he battles his own demons and seeks help in rebuilding his life. Marianne continues to offer Connell support after she returns to Sweden.

programme.title: NHK World English News
programme.desc: English news from Japan's Broadcasting Corporation, NHK, delivering the latest in business, technology, health, environmental and world news.

programme.title: Al Jazeera News Hour
programme.desc: In-depth global news from Al Jazeera Satellite Network, Doha, Qatar, in English.

programme.title: New York Gourmet With Justine Schofield
programme.desc: S1 E5 Justine visits another iconic Buffalo venue for a traditional roast beef lunch before setting off for the breathtaking 1000 Islands, visiting scenic spots like Boldt Castle and Morgan Island.

programme.title: Memory Bites with Matt Moran
programme.desc: S1 E5 Courtney Act Chef Matt Moran delves into the food memories of multifaceted entertainer Courtney Act, revealing how retro family dishes and deep resilience have illuminated their path to stardom.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Seafood Odyssey
programme.desc: S1 E1 Suffolk and Naples Contemplating life over a bottle of wine against the backdrop of the bay of Naples, Rick has found the perfect place, and person, to start his seafood odyssey.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Seafood Odyssey
programme.desc: S1 E2 India and Cornwall Rick flees the restaurant to seek comfort from the sea. Forty-eight kilometres out of Padstow, he calms down. Veteran fisherman Ivan Bates introduces Rick to the joys of fishing for the best fish in the world, turbot.

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: S22 E7 South Wales: Richard It's the second night of the competition and the turn of account executive Ricard to host, not in his house but next door in the pub he runs with his partner.

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: S22 E8 South Wales: Daffyd Third to host in South Wales is hotel receptionist and aspiring personal trainer Daffyd, who's hosting a healthy vegetarian-ish dinner party, as he hopes to impress his guests.

programme.title: The Cook Up with Adam Liaw
programme.desc: S7 E81 Tinned Tomatoes A pantry staple becomes the hero tonight as Adam and his guests, comedian Mel Buttle and chef Dom Wilton make magic with tinned tomatoes.

programme.title: The Cook and the Chef
programme.desc: S4 E12 The Art of Presentation Maggie gives us a snapshot on the world of food photography, one which is often veiled in trickery, sprays, glues and gels, all used to artificially enhance the look of a dish. Maggie's approach is a bit different: self trained, she likes to keep her style simple and natural, letting the food speak for itself and the skills of the photographer really shine through.

programme.title: Paula McIntyre's Hamely Kitchen
programme.desc: S2 E1 Paula adds a modern twist to a traditional roozle breid, a variation on potato bread, by transforming it into a taco.

programme.title: Home Cooking Made Easy
programme.desc: S1 E3 Entertaining Lorraine prepares a gorgeous, hearty Spanish paella with sherry, chorizo, and prawns - the ideal one-pan 'help yourself dish' for a fun night in with friends and family.

programme.title: Pati's Mexican Table
programme.desc: S12 E9 Pink An ingredient Pati constantly uses is salt and Yucatan has one of the most unique salts. The Las Coloradas salt, which means blush red, gets its distinctive color from red algae. Engineer Felipe Perez takes Pati to the pink lakes where the salt is produced. Down the road in Rio Lagartos, conservationist Diego Nunez takes her to see another pink wonder, Mexico's highest concentration of flamingos.

programme.title: David Rocco's Dolce Italia
programme.desc: S1 E2 Old Venice on the Water David sets out with his family to get the true Venice tourist experience and meets a charming gondolier and his wife, who teach them all about the history and pride of the age-old tradition of the gondolas in Venice. They explore local hotspots and venture off the beaten path to a beautiful Venetian winery, sampling gourmet cicchetti along the way. David then spends time with Emanuel, a local fisherman,.

programme.title: Island Echoes with Nornie Bero
programme.desc: S1 E8 Echoes of Erub In the final episode of Season 1 of Island Echoes, Nornie Bero visits the breathtaking island of Erub to experience a truly unique local pastime.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing: Simply Provence
programme.desc: S1 E9 Chocolate There is one delicious food that is adored across the world. It may have started life in South America as the humble cocoa bean, but it's the Swiss, Belgians and French, who've turned it into an ingredient we all adore.

programme.title: My Market Kitchen
programme.desc: S6 E19 Mike is joined by his daughter Abigail to whip up her favourite treat, double chocolate cookies. Matt creates a Vietnamese dessert, coconut creme caramel. Laura wraps up the show with carbonara.

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen
programme.desc: S8 E8 Wheat Harvest and Pasta Lidia talks the hard work involved with making flour, then bread and pasta. She makes croutons with a Caesar salad, then a fusilli with spinach and herbed ricotta, and a lagane pasta with chickpeas.

programme.title: Tastes And Traditions
programme.desc: S1 E9 In this cozy episode of Tastes and Traditions, we revisit two timeless classics of Ukrainian home cooking-warm, fragrant Cabbage Buns and juicy Pork Cutlets.

programme.title: Jamie at Home
programme.desc: S1 E9 Pizza Jamie searches for edible wild mushrooms in a local forest with his mentor, Gennaro Contaldo. Then he uses them to make bruschetta, risotto and venison Stroganoff.

programme.title: Food Safari
programme.desc: S1 E3 Portuguese Maeve O'Meara takes you on a journey within your very own kitchen and makes new flavours familiar. In tonight's episode, Maeve explores the world of Portuguese food.

programme.title: The Chocolate Queen
programme.desc: S2 E6 Warm apple tarts are hard to resist and pastry expert Kirsten Tibballs is in the kitchen showing her version that's easy to replicate at home. She's also dishing up a brilliant no-churn chocolate, date and ice cream cake that is better than anything you'll find in the store.

programme.title: Everyday Gourmet with Justine Schofield
programme.desc: S4 E33 Justine makes her sweet potato and ginger gratin, gives you some great tips for steaming eggs and Adam Liaw makes his leche flan.

programme.title: Herrhausen: The Banker & The Bomb
programme.desc: S1 E2 When Herrhausen's initial attempts to broker a deal with the USSR fail, German Chancellor Helmut Kohl calls him back to Berlin under a cloud of embarrassment. However, when the seismic Black Monday crash causes economic chaos in America and across the word, Herrhausen's bold ideas are suddenly vindicated. Emboldened by Herrhausen's new status as a visionary, Kohl seizes the opportunity to make a fresh approach with Moscow. Yet Herrhausen's enemies still lurk in the shadows.

programme.title: Gomorrah
programme.desc: S1 E10 Major bloodshed, if not all-out war with Salvatore Conte, is imminent when Conte returns to Naples to get to the bottom to avenge Giuliano's murder. Meanwhile, Ciro weaves his web further and further around Genny to distract from the rat he is beginning to smell. If it wasn't Genny who gave the order, he must join in on the manhunt for Daniel to prove his own innocence.

programme.title: Gomorrah
programme.desc: S1 E11 What all bosses had tried to avoid is now the dire truth: Daniele's death sparks an entire series of bloodshed. All clans opposing or holding grudges against the Savastanos rally around Conte, forcing Genny to cut all ties to him he had still been upholding for strategic reasons. Not ending there, Genny now virtually faces a civil war on the inside of his own clan: a deadly battle between his own boys and the old lieutenants.

programme.title: Gomorrah
programme.desc: S1 E12 While Daniele's death may have caused bloodshed, Imma's death leads to open warfare in the streets. So when the pavement reaches boiling point, even Ciro has to flee to Rome with his wife and daughter. Both clans barricade themselves in their apartment bunkers, waiting for the enemy in a lethal stalemate. When squadrons of police arrive at the scene, it is the last straw that breaks the camel's back.

programme.title: Pati's Mexican Table

Down the road in Rio Lagartos, conservationist Diego Nunez takes her to see another pink wonder, Mexico's highest concentration of flamingos.

programme.desc: S1 E1 Suffolk and Naples Contemplating life over a bottle of wine against the backdrop of the bay of Naples, Rick has found the perfect place, and person, to start his seafood odyssey.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Seafood Odyssey
programme.desc: S1 E2 India and Cornwall Rick flees the restaurant to seek comfort from the sea. Forty-eight kilometres out of Padstow, he calms down. Veteran fisherman Ivan Bates introduces Rick to the joys of fishing for the best fish in the world, turbot.

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: S22 E7 South Wales: Richard It's the second night of the competition and the turn of account executive Ricard to host, not in his house but next door in the pub he runs with his partner.

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: S22 E8 South Wales: Daffyd Third to host in South Wales is hotel receptionist and aspiring personal trainer Daffyd, who's hosting a healthy vegetarian-ish dinner party, as he hopes to impress his guests.

programme.title: The Cook Up with Adam Liaw
programme.desc: S7 E81 Tinned Tomatoes A pantry staple becomes the hero tonight as Adam and his guests, comedian Mel Buttle and chef Dom Wilton make magic with tinned tomatoes.

programme.title: The Cook and the Chef
programme.desc: S4 E12 The Art of Presentation Maggie gives us a snapshot on the world of food photography, one which is often veiled in trickery, sprays, glues and gels, all used to artificially enhance the look of a dish. Maggie's approach is a bit different: self trained, she likes to keep her style simple and natural, letting the food speak for itself and the skills of the photographer really shine through.

programme.title: Paula McIntyre's Hamely Kitchen
programme.desc: S2 E1 Paula adds a modern twist to a traditional roozle breid, a variation on potato bread, by transforming it into a taco.

programme.title: Home Cooking Made Easy
programme.desc: S1 E3 Entertaining Lorraine prepares a gorgeous, hearty Spanish paella with sherry, chorizo, and prawns - the ideal one-pan 'help yourself dish' for a fun night in with friends and family.

programme.title: Pati's Mexican Table
programme.desc: S12 E9 Pink An ingredient Pati constantly uses is salt and Yucatan has one of the most unique salts. The Las Coloradas salt, which means blush red, gets its distinctive color from red algae. Engineer Felipe Perez takes Pati to the pink lakes where the salt is produced. Down the road in Rio Lagartos, conservationist Diego Nunez takes her to see another pink wonder, Mexico's highest concentration of flamingos.

programme.title: David Rocco's Dolce Italia
programme.desc: S1 E2 Old Venice on the Water David sets out with his family to get the true Venice tourist experience and meets a charming gondolier and his wife, who teach them all about the history and pride of the age-old tradition of the gondolas in Venice. They explore local hotspots and venture off the beaten path to a beautiful Venetian winery, sampling gourmet cicchetti along the way. David then spends time with Emanuel, a local fisherman,.

programme.title: Island Echoes with Nornie Bero
programme.desc: S1 E8 Echoes of Erub In the final episode of Season 1 of Island Echoes, Nornie Bero visits the breathtaking island of Erub to experience a truly unique local pastime.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing: Simply Provence
programme.desc: S1 E9 Chocolate There is one delicious food that is adored across the world. It may have started life in South America as the humble cocoa bean, but it's the Swiss, Belgians and French, who've turned it into an ingredient we all adore.

programme.title: My Market Kitchen
programme.desc: S6 E19 Mike is joined by his daughter Abigail to whip up her favourite treat, double chocolate cookies. Matt creates a Vietnamese dessert, coconut creme caramel. Laura wraps up the show with carbonara.

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen
programme.desc: S8 E8 Wheat Harvest and Pasta Lidia talks the hard work involved with making flour, then bread and pasta. She makes croutons with a Caesar salad, then a fusilli with spinach and herbed ricotta, and a lagane pasta with chickpeas.

programme.title: Tastes And Traditions
programme.desc: S1 E9 In this cozy episode of Tastes and Traditions, we revisit two timeless classics of Ukrainian home cooking-warm, fragrant Cabbage Buns and juicy Pork Cutlets.

programme.title: Jamie at Home
programme.desc: S1 E9 Pizza Jamie searches for edible wild mushrooms in a local forest with his mentor, Gennaro Contaldo. Then he uses them to make bruschetta, risotto and venison Stroganoff.

programme.title: Food Safari
programme.desc: S1 E3 Portuguese Maeve O'Meara takes you on a journey within your very own kitchen and makes new flavours familiar. In tonight's episode, Maeve explores the world of Portuguese food.

programme.title: The Chocolate Queen
programme.desc: S2 E6 Warm apple tarts are hard to resist and pastry expert Kirsten Tibballs is in the kitchen showing her version that's easy to replicate at home. She's also dishing up a brilliant no-churn chocolate, date and ice cream cake that is better than anything you'll find in the store.

programme.title: Everyday Gourmet with Justine Schofield
programme.desc: S4 E33 Justine makes her sweet potato and ginger gratin, gives you some great tips for steaming eggs and Adam Liaw makes his leche flan.

After teaching Pati the ins and outs of the game, Dona Enedina invites her over for Brazo de Reina, a tamal with hardboiled eggs and ground pepitas.

Together, this group of expatriates act as the young boy's surrogate mothers, watching over him as they all weather the rise of fascism, the menacing political climate, and impending personal heartbreak.

programme.title: Dead Again
programme.desc: A woman who has lost her memory is taken in by a Los Angeles orphanage, and private eye Mike Church is enlisted to track down her identity. However, Mike soon finds that he might have a past life connection to the woman that endangers both their lives.

programme.title: John Wick: Chapter 2
programme.desc: Bound by a blood oath to help legendary hit man John Wick travels to Rome where he squares off against the deadliest killers.

programme.title: Mamacruz
programme.desc: A religious grandmother learns how to use the internet. When she accidentally comes across pornography, she is faced with a dilemma.

programme.title: The Orator
programme.desc: This acclaimed film is the first entirely produced and shot in Samoa. Saili, a taro farmer with dwarfism, attempts to reclaim his father's chief status, despite the current village chief's scepticism. Saili must prove his oratory skills are good enough to lead the community, and must speak up to defend the ones he loves.

programme.title: A Hazard Of Hearts
programme.desc: A beautiful young woman is sent to a cliff-top mansion after her father loses her and his estate in a wager. Based on the novel by Barbara Cartland.

programme.title: Tea With Mussolini
programme.desc: A phenomenal cast of accomplished actresses help make famed director Franco Zeffirelli's semi-autobiographical tale an enchanting and warm film. A boy whose mother has died and whose father has all but abandoned him is raised by an eccentric, caustically witty group of older British and American women in 1930s Florence. Together, this group of expatriates act as the young boy's surrogate mothers, watching over him as they all weather the rise of fascism, the menacing political climate, and impending personal heartbreak.

programme.title: In a Land that no Longer Exists
programme.desc: Exploring fashion in the former GDR, this film highlights iconic Sibylle magazine, state brand Exquisit, and the underground creative subculture behind East Germany's style scene.

programme.title: Two Many Chefs
programme.desc: A driven chef's shot at a third Michelin star is upended when his estranged, amnesiac father joins his kitchen- just as the King of Spain books a table. Past and present collide in chaos.

programme.title: The Most Beautiful Day in the World
programme.desc: Arturo must take care of Gioele and Rebecca, two children inherited from an old uncle. When he discovers Gioele has superpowers, his luck changes.

programme.title: Buckley's Chance
programme.desc: After the loss of his father, the young boy Ridley is forced to move to the Australian outback to live with his estranged Grandfather. During his adventures he becomes lost and befriends a dingo excluded from its own pack. A strong bond is formed in the harsh Australian outback as the two try to make their way home.

programme.title: Thunderbirds Are GO
programme.desc: A 21st-century astronaut and his sons hunt for the saboteur plotting against a proposed flight to Mars.

programme.title: The Way Of The Dragon
programme.desc: Tang Lung is a young man who travels to Rome to help a family friend whose restaurant is being targeted by the local Mafia. After driving off the local thugs, the stakes are raised as Tang must confront several martial arts experts hired by the crime boss, including karate champion Colt.

programme.title: The Big Boss
programme.desc: Cheng, a young Chinese man sworn to an oath of non-violence, is sent to live in Thailand with his uncle and cousins. His promise to his mother not to fight is repeatedly tested when he goes to work in the local icehouse for an abusive overseer. When some of his cousins are killed, after discovering the icehouse is actually a front for a heroin-smuggling operation, Cheng sets out to exact revenge.

programme.title: Syriana
programme.desc: A politically charged epic about the state of the oil industry in the hands of those personally involved and affected by it.

programme.title: Dead Again
programme.desc: A woman who has lost her memory is taken in by a Los Angeles orphanage, and private eye Mike Church is enlisted to track down her identity. However, Mike soon finds that he might have a past life connection to the woman that endangers both their lives.

programme.title: Radioactive
programme.desc: After the death of her beloved husband, Marie Curie's commitment to science remains strong as she tries to explain previously unknown radioactive elements. But it soon becomes terrifyingly evident that her work could lead to applications in medicine that could save thousands of lives - or applications in warfare that could destroy them by the billions.

programme.title: New York Gourmet With Justine Schofield
programme.desc: S1 E5 Justine visits another iconic Buffalo venue for a traditional roast beef lunch before setting off for the breathtaking 1000 Islands, visiting scenic spots like Boldt Castle and Morgan Island.

programme.title: Memory Bites with Matt Moran
programme.desc: S1 E5 Courtney Act Chef Matt Moran delves into the food memories of multifaceted entertainer Courtney Act, revealing how retro family dishes and deep resilience have illuminated their path to stardom.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Seafood Odyssey
programme.desc: S1 E1 Suffolk and Naples Contemplating life over a bottle of wine against the backdrop of the bay of Naples, Rick has found the perfect place, and person, to start his seafood odyssey.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Seafood Odyssey
programme.desc: S1 E2 India and Cornwall Rick flees the restaurant to seek comfort from the sea. Forty-eight kilometres out of Padstow, he calms down. Veteran fisherman Ivan Bates introduces Rick to the joys of fishing for the best fish in the world, turbot.

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: S22 E7 South Wales: Richard It's the second night of the competition and the turn of account executive Ricard to host, not in his house but next door in the pub he runs with his partner.

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: S22 E8 South Wales: Daffyd Third to host in South Wales is hotel receptionist and aspiring personal trainer Daffyd, who's hosting a healthy vegetarian-ish dinner party, as he hopes to impress his guests.

programme.title: The Cook Up with Adam Liaw
programme.desc: S7 E81 Tinned Tomatoes A pantry staple becomes the hero tonight as Adam and his guests, comedian Mel Buttle and chef Dom Wilton make magic with tinned tomatoes.

programme.title: The Cook and the Chef
programme.desc: S4 E12 The Art of Presentation Maggie gives us a snapshot on the world of food photography, one which is often veiled in trickery, sprays, glues and gels, all used to artificially enhance the look of a dish. Maggie's approach is a bit different: self trained, she likes to keep her style simple and natural, letting the food speak for itself and the skills of the photographer really shine through.

programme.title: Paula McIntyre's Hamely Kitchen
programme.desc: S2 E1 Paula adds a modern twist to a traditional roozle breid, a variation on potato bread, by transforming it into a taco.

programme.title: Home Cooking Made Easy
programme.desc: S1 E3 Entertaining Lorraine prepares a gorgeous, hearty Spanish paella with sherry, chorizo, and prawns - the ideal one-pan 'help yourself dish' for a fun night in with friends and family.

programme.title: Pati's Mexican Table
programme.desc: S12 E9 Pink An ingredient Pati constantly uses is salt and Yucatan has one of the most unique salts. The Las Coloradas salt, which means blush red, gets its distinctive color from red algae. Engineer Felipe Perez takes Pati to the pink lakes where the salt is produced. Down the road in Rio Lagartos, conservationist Diego Nunez takes her to see another pink wonder, Mexico's highest concentration of flamingos.

programme.title: David Rocco's Dolce Italia
programme.desc: S1 E2 Old Venice on the Water David sets out with his family to get the true Venice tourist experience and meets a charming gondolier and his wife, who teach them all about the history and pride of the age-old tradition of the gondolas in Venice. They explore local hotspots and venture off the beaten path to a beautiful Venetian winery, sampling gourmet cicchetti along the way. David then spends time with Emanuel, a local fisherman,.

programme.title: Island Echoes with Nornie Bero
programme.desc: S1 E8 Echoes of Erub In the final episode of Season 1 of Island Echoes, Nornie Bero visits the breathtaking island of Erub to experience a truly unique local pastime.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing: Simply Provence
programme.desc: S1 E9 Chocolate There is one delicious food that is adored across the world. It may have started life in South America as the humble cocoa bean, but it's the Swiss, Belgians and French, who've turned it into an ingredient we all adore.

programme.title: My Market Kitchen
programme.desc: S6 E19 Mike is joined by his daughter Abigail to whip up her favourite treat, double chocolate cookies. Matt creates a Vietnamese dessert, coconut creme caramel. Laura wraps up the show with carbonara.

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen
programme.desc: S8 E8 Wheat Harvest and Pasta Lidia talks the hard work involved with making flour, then bread and pasta. She makes croutons with a Caesar salad, then a fusilli with spinach and herbed ricotta, and a lagane pasta with chickpeas.

programme.title: Tastes And Traditions
programme.desc: S1 E9 In this cozy episode of Tastes and Traditions, we revisit two timeless classics of Ukrainian home cooking-warm, fragrant Cabbage Buns and juicy Pork Cutlets.

programme.title: Jamie at Home
programme.desc: S1 E9 Pizza Jamie searches for edible wild mushrooms in a local forest with his mentor, Gennaro Contaldo. Then he uses them to make bruschetta, risotto and venison Stroganoff.

programme.title: Food Safari
programme.desc: S1 E3 Portuguese Maeve O'Meara takes you on a journey within your very own kitchen and makes new flavours familiar. In tonight's episode, Maeve explores the world of Portuguese food.

programme.title: The Chocolate Queen
programme.desc: S2 E6 Warm apple tarts are hard to resist and pastry expert Kirsten Tibballs is in the kitchen showing her version that's easy to replicate at home. She's also dishing up a brilliant no-churn chocolate, date and ice cream cake that is better than anything you'll find in the store.

programme.title: Everyday Gourmet with Justine Schofield
programme.desc: S4 E33 Justine makes her sweet potato and ginger gratin, gives you some great tips for steaming eggs and Adam Liaw makes his leche flan.

The Honeymooners, The Andy Griffith Show and Roseanne all offer funny snapshots at class divisions in America, divisions that are even starker in Arrested Development and Schitt's Creek. But it is It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia that asks the hardest, perhaps funniest question of all - is this aspirational game we're all playing rigged against us?

Down the road in Rio Lagartos, conservationist Diego Nunez takes her to see another pink wonder, Mexico's highest concentration of flamingos.

programme.title: David Rocco's Dolce Italia

programme.title: Pioneers of Love
programme.desc: S1 E1 Recounts the epic saga and follows the lives of Leandro Illin and a Ngadjon woman, Kitty Clarke, a traditional owner of the land. Pioneers of Love begins by telling the story of how, in 1910, the Illins, a family of aristocratic Russian dissidents, fled to Australia to escape persecution. Tropical north Queensland is where Leandro met Kitty, a 20-year-old widow with three children and this program tells the story of Leandro and Kitty's battle to be granted permission to be recognised as husband and wife and the backlash they received because of this request. In the midst of this, xenophobia began to sweep Australia. (Commissioned by SBS, in English) (Documentary) (Part 1 of 2) (Rpt) PG CC WS.

programme.title: Grand Designs Australia
programme.desc: S10 E16 Coober Pedy 'Dug Out, SA From deep underground, to high on a bushfire-prone mountain top, Grand Designs Series 10B is a testament to the lengths, depths and heights some of Australia's most ambitious and passionate home owners will strive for to realise their dreams. From shipping containers, to dugouts, a 100 year old hat factory, to a solid concrete bunker, this season sees homeowners push the limits in their quest to find clever design solutions in some of the most extreme environments on the planet. From the soaring temperatures of Coober Pedy, to the windswept coastline of South Australia's Fleurieu Peninsula; the surfer paradise of Torquay, Victoria, to Sydney's bustling inner city hotspot of Newtown; host Peter Maddison goes on a journey of discovery, surprise and some trepidation with some of Australia's boldest architectural trailblazers. Astounding designs, innovative materials, inspired solutions in some of the best locations in the country. Grand Designs Australia Series 10 - you haven't seen anything like it.

programme.title: Ice Road Truckers
programme.desc: S10 E5 The Rookie For two months out of every year, a group of exceptional men find their way to the Canadian tundra to undertake one of the most dangerous jobs on Earth. In the thick of winter, truckers in giant 18-wheelers carry vital equipment and supplies to miners hundreds of miles away. In blizzard conditions, these truckers travel over ice roads that often take them over frozen lakes. Each man is trained in self survival, from fixing his truck in sub-zero conditions in seconds to escaping from a truck if the ice cracks. On the other end of the journey are miners whose lives depend on the truckers making it to their base, year after year.

programme.title: Outback Truckers
programme.desc: S2 E4 Episode 4 This vast island continent is home to some of the hardest places to reach on Earth. But for the mega trucks that keep the country moving, getting there is just another day at the office. Longer than a jet liner and heavier than a tank, they can run 24/7, pulling anything from houses to hamburgers. Behind the wheel are some of the best and toughest drivers in the world, their motto: anything, anytime, anywhere. Turbo embarks on a journey through an area affected by bush fires, and Yogi faces the biggest week of his career.

programme.title: Inside the Factory
programme.desc: S3 E1 Tea Bags Gregg Wallace receives a load of tea leaves from Kenya and follows their journey through the factory that produces one-quarter of all the tea drunk in Britain. Gregg turns his 20-tonne batch into 6.9 million bags. Along the way, he discovers that there can be up to 20 different teas in your bag and that the recipe for the blend is altered every day, measured against a standard created in 1978. Meanwhile, Cherry Healey discovers the secrets of the tea leaf in an African tea-processing plant. She learns that 40 percent of each leaf is made up of chemicals called polyphenols. She is surprised to find that white, green and black tea are all made from the same leaves. She also discovers that the bag surrounding your tea is not ordinary paper, but a highly-engineered fabric made up of hemp, wood and polypropylene. She watches as a 60km-long roll is produced, and she gets some scientific tips on making the best possible cup of tea with a tea bag. Historian Ruth Goodman investigates tea adulteration. In the 19th-century, there were eight separate factories in London which existed solely to dry and recolour used tea leaves. She discovers that it was 'honest' John Hornim who put that right and ensured we could trust our tea. She also finds that in the military during WWII, armoured divisions had to leave the safety of their tanks to brew-up, a habit that resulted in many casualties. She climbs on board a modern-day tank to make a cup of tea with a boiling vessel, the innovation that solved this problem.

programme.title: Inside the Factory
programme.desc: S3 E2 Pasta Gregg Wallace is in Italy, hitching a lift on a train carrying more than 1000 tonnes of wheat to the largest dried pasta factory in the world. It produces 60 percent of all pasta made in Italy and supplies 3000 tonnes to the UK each year. Gregg traces the journey the wheat takes through a seven-storey mill and into the production zone where it is mixed with water, pushed through moulds and turned into spaghetti. Along the way, he discovers that the perfect string of spaghetti is 25cm long and examines the technology that allows them to produce 150,000km of it each day, enough to stretch round the Earth almost four times. Meanwhile, Cherry Healey discovers why the best pasta is made with durum wheat. This is a hard wheat that, when it is milled, turns into the granular yellow flour known as semolina, which translates as semi-milled. This is the essential basis of pasta as it retains its shape and texture when cooked. She also helps to harvest 15 tonnes of tomatoes, turning them into 3000L of pasta sauce. Along the way, Cherry is surprised to hear that the British habit of pairing spaghetti with bolognese outrages many Italians. She learns why different shapes of pasta are ideally paired with different sauces, and promises in future she will serve her spaghetti with a more suitable topping, like carbonara. Historian Ruth Goodman discovers that pasta arrived in Britain much earlier than we imagined. She heads to the British Library to look at a manuscript from 1390, a cookbook written for King Richard II which contains a recipe for something called lozyns. Ruth cooks up a batch and is convinced that this an early version of lasagne. She also navigates the streets of Soho armed with a 1958 restaurant guide to find out how we first fell in love with Italian food.

programme.title: Location Location Location
programme.desc: S16 E1 West London Kirstie and Phil are in West London helping two couples find their dream first homes in this perilous property market. Not only is property expensive here, but it often sells in record time so Phil and Kirstie will need to summon all their property know-how if they want to be the first over the finish line. Dance-mad newlyweds Keon and Zoe are taking their first step onto the London property ladder and are looking for a family home with space for future children and room for their favourite hobby, salsa dancing. They are renting in Shepherd's Bush and would love to stay in the area, but even with their healthy budget of 450,000 pounds, Phil has the ultimate challenge on his hands if he's to find them all the space they want in this pricey patch. Kirstie is a little further west in the borough of Richmond, helping Carolyn and Paul who are also looking to buy their first home together. Paul has bought property before in his native Sheffield and is struggling to get his head around the price of property in the capital. They have a budget of 325,000 pounds and for that, Carolyn is desperate for somewhere with outside space so she can dry her delicates on the washing line. Will Kirstie be able to help this couple find their dream home at the right price?

programme.title: Forensic Files
programme.desc: S2 E1 The Common Thread Ten bodies had been found between the months of May and November of 1984 in Florida. The police discovered several similarities among these cases. Red carpet fibres had been found on all the bodies, some of the victims were found near tire tracks, and some had hair samples from the perpetrator. It wasn't until November 3, 1984, that the case began to unfold as the perpetrator abducted a 17-year-old female named Lisa McVey. Once released by her kidnapper, McVey ran to the police with information, such as interior descriptions of his car and a possible ATM he had been to, that eventually led to the killer's arrest.

programme.title: Forensic Files
programme.desc: S2 E2 The Dirty Deed On November 18, 1993 friends of Eileen and Derek Severs called and notified the police that the couple had been missing for several days. The police searched the Savers' home and questioned their son Roger who had recently moved in with his parents. Although the bodies had not yet been found, Police arrested and detained Roger on suspicions of murdering his parents. Only after finding blood samples in Eileen's car and careful analysis of the mud flaps on Derek's car, were the police able to determine where Roger had buried his parents. Roger had used his mother's car to discard incriminating evidence and used his father's car to transport the bodies to the burial site.

programme.desc: S1 E2 The Magic Bullet Fifteen-year-old Trey Cooley dies from a mysterious gunshot wound to the head while he sits in the lobby of his father's gun club. Gumshoe investigation, ballistics, laser technology, made-to-scale models and the latest in forensic animation determine that the bullet that killed him followed a tragic course after a misfire at the outdoor range.

programme.title: Forensic Files
programme.desc: S1 E3 The House That Roared Caren Campano disappears, and her husband's story doesn't hold up. Police find a large stain on the Campanos' bedroom carpet. They use a chemical called luminol that reveals a room spattered with blood which, when cleaned off, could not be seen by the naked eye. Complex reverse paternity tests of Caren's relatives match her blood type to the blood on the carpet. The evidence convicts Chris Campano of murder. The body isn't found until a year later.

programme.title: Forensic Files
programme.desc: S1 E4 The Footpath Murders English detectives team up with a pioneering scientist to crack a case of sexual assault and serial murder. In 1983, a quiet country village is gripped with fear as authorities search for the killer of 15-year-old Lynda Mann. Clueless, they start again when Dawn Ashworth is killed three years later. They enlist the help of Dr Alec Jeffreys, a molecular biologist who uses his breakthrough technique of genetic fingerprinting to rule out one suspect by comparing his DNA with that of semen found on the victims' bodies. Police set up a DNA dragnet to trap and convict the real killer. This 1986 murder case is the first to use DNA as evidence in a criminal case.

programme.title: Forensic Files
programme.desc: S1 E5 Planted Evidence Police in Arizona ask a molecular geneticist to pick out a tree in a line-up when unidentified seed pods are found in a suspect's truck. The judge rules into evidence DNA profiles linking the pods to a tree near where the body was found. Increasingly, non-human DNA is making its way into the court system.

programme.title: Forensic Files
programme.desc: S2 E3 Killer Fog One particular stretch of road on Interstate 75 seems to be accident-prone, adding up to seven multi-car accidents in 15 years. Each accident was caused by a sudden and impenetrable fog, which forced drivers to suddenly break without concern for those behind them. Environmental experts and investigators analysed the elements of nature occurring during this unnatural thick fog and tried to determine possible water sources that could create so many vapours in the air. They found one particular paper plant near the interstate that releases significant water vapours, which react to the weather and create this deadly fog.

From the soaring temperatures of Coober Pedy, to the windswept coastline of South Australia's Fleurieu Peninsula; the surfer paradise of Torquay, Victoria, to Sydney's bustling inner city hotspot of Newtown; host Peter Maddison goes on a journey of discovery, surprise and some trepidation with some of Australia's boldest architectural trailblazers. Fitness instructor Kim is on a one woman mission to get her lorry driving husband, Martin, eating healthily when he's not on the road. programme.title: Inside the Factory
programme.desc: S3 E1 Tea Bags Gregg Wallace receives a load of tea leaves from Kenya and follows their journey through the factory that produces one-quarter of all the tea drunk in Britain. Gregg turns his 20-tonne batch into 6.9 million bags. Along the way, he discovers that there can be up to 20 different teas in your bag and that the recipe for the blend is altered every day, measured against a standard created in 1978. Meanwhile, Cherry Healey discovers the secrets of the tea leaf in an African tea-processing plant. She learns that 40 percent of each leaf is made up of chemicals called polyphenols. She is surprised to find that white, green and black tea are all made from the same leaves. She also discovers that the bag surrounding your tea is not ordinary paper, but a highly-engineered fabric made up of hemp, wood and polypropylene. She watches as a 60km-long roll is produced, and she gets some scientific tips on making the best possible cup of tea with a tea bag. Historian Ruth Goodman investigates tea adulteration. In the 19th-century, there were eight separate factories in London which existed solely to dry and recolour used tea leaves. She discovers that it was 'honest' John Hornim who put that right and ensured we could trust our tea. She also finds that in the military during WWII, armoured divisions had to leave the safety of their tanks to brew-up, a habit that resulted in many casualties. She climbs on board a modern-day tank to make a cup of tea with a boiling vessel, the innovation that solved this problem.

programme.title: Inside the Factory
programme.desc: S3 E2 Pasta Gregg Wallace is in Italy, hitching a lift on a train carrying more than 1000 tonnes of wheat to the largest dried pasta factory in the world. It produces 60 percent of all pasta made in Italy and supplies 3000 tonnes to the UK each year. Gregg traces the journey the wheat takes through a seven-storey mill and into the production zone where it is mixed with water, pushed through moulds and turned into spaghetti. Along the way, he discovers that the perfect string of spaghetti is 25cm long and examines the technology that allows them to produce 150,000km of it each day, enough to stretch round the Earth almost four times. Meanwhile, Cherry Healey discovers why the best pasta is made with durum wheat. This is a hard wheat that, when it is milled, turns into the granular yellow flour known as semolina, which translates as semi-milled. This is the essential basis of pasta as it retains its shape and texture when cooked. She also helps to harvest 15 tonnes of tomatoes, turning them into 3000L of pasta sauce. Along the way, Cherry is surprised to hear that the British habit of pairing spaghetti with bolognese outrages many Italians. She learns why different shapes of pasta are ideally paired with different sauces, and promises in future she will serve her spaghetti with a more suitable topping, like carbonara. Historian Ruth Goodman discovers that pasta arrived in Britain much earlier than we imagined. programme.title: Inside the Factory
programme.desc: S3 E2 Pasta Gregg Wallace is in Italy, hitching a lift on a train carrying more than 1000 tonnes of wheat to the largest dried pasta factory in the world. It produces 60 percent of all pasta made in Italy and supplies 3000 tonnes to the UK each year. Gregg traces the journey the wheat takes through a seven-storey mill and into the production zone where it is mixed with water, pushed through moulds and turned into spaghetti. Along the way, he discovers that the perfect string of spaghetti is 25cm long and examines the technology that allows them to produce 150,000km of it each day, enough to stretch round the Earth almost four times. Meanwhile, Cherry Healey discovers why the best pasta is made with durum wheat. This is a hard wheat that, when it is milled, turns into the granular yellow flour known as semolina, which translates as semi-milled. This is the essential basis of pasta as it retains its shape and texture when cooked. She also helps to harvest 15 tonnes of tomatoes, turning them into 3000L of pasta sauce. Along the way, Cherry is surprised to hear that the British habit of pairing spaghetti with bolognese outrages many Italians. She learns why different shapes of pasta are ideally paired with different sauces, and promises in future she will serve her spaghetti with a more suitable topping, like carbonara. Historian Ruth Goodman discovers that pasta arrived in Britain much earlier than we imagined. She heads to the British Library to look at a manuscript from 1390, a cookbook written for King Richard II which contains a recipe for something called lozyns. Ruth cooks up a batch and is convinced that this an early version of lasagne. She also navigates the streets of Soho armed with a 1958 restaurant guide to find out how we first fell in love with Italian food.

When four high-school kids discover an old video game console with a game they've never heard of Jumanji they are immediately drawn into the game's jungle setting, literally becoming the avatars they chose: gamer Spencer becomes a brawny adventurer; football jock Fridge loses (in his words) 'the top two feet of his body' and becomes an Einstein; popular girl Bethany becomes a middle-aged male professor; and wallflower Martha becomes a badass warrior. What they discover is that you don't just play Jumanji you must survive it. To beat the game and return to the real world, they'll have to go on the most dangerous adventure of their lives, discover what Alan Parrish left 20 years ago, and change the way they think about themselves or they'll be stuck in the game forever.

Valenti, to show the world that family can come from the most unexpected places and there's nothing wrong with a big singing crocodile with an even bigger personality.
